channel.title: The Catholic Review - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from The Catholic Review (catholicreview.org)

item.title: Movie Review: ‘Wuthering Heights’
item.description: “Barbie” meets “Bridgerton” in "'Wuthering Heights,'" the latest screen version of the beloved 1847 novel by Emily Bronte.

item.title: Students from L.A.-area Catholic school get surprise meeting with pope after school vandalism
item.description: Msgr. Figueiredo was able to arrange for the group to receive an audience with Pope Leo and to have their school be named during the ceremony.

item.title: U.S.-led Board of Peace a ‘colonialist operation,’ Cardinal Pizzaballa says
item.description: Cardinal Pierbattista Pizzaballa, Latin patriarch of Jerusalem, strongly criticized the U.S.-led Board of Peace, an international body chaired by President Donald Trump to oversee the governance and reconstruction of Gaza.

item.title: Deadly mass shooting at Rhode Island hockey match may have involved ‘family dispute’
item.description: A deadly shooting erupted during a boys hockey game in Rhode Island, involving a co-op with a number of players reported to be from an area Catholic school, and may have been motivated by what law enforcement characterized as a "family dispute."

item.title: Data on sweeping immigrant detentions underscores U.S. bishops’ concerns, says policy expert
item.description: Data showing most individuals in immigration detention do not have violent criminal records highlights ongoing concerns expressed by the nation's Catholic bishops over the Trump administration immigration crackdown, said an official with the U.S. Conference of Catholic Bishops.

item.title: ‘Remember you are dust’: Why people fill the pew on Ash Wednesday
item.description: Why do so many people make an extra effort to get to church on Ash Wednesday -- the first of Lent's 40 days -- when it is not a holy day of obligation, and they are not required to receive ashes?

item.title: Stepping up to Lent
item.description: Everything we love, cherish and enjoy -- the best and most meaningful experiences we remember all our lives -- require people who are willing to spend their resources, share their talents and work their tails off to make them happen.

item.title: Commission issues ‘painful’ abuse report on Polish diocese, a first in the crisis-hit nation
item.description: A newly released clerical sexual abuse report in Poland's Diocese of Sosnowiec is being described by investigators as a necessary step toward accountability, while Church leaders call it a painful but essential moment in rebuilding trust after years of scandals.

item.title: From Foreheads to Crowns: How Ash Wednesday looks different worldwide
item.description: Catholics going to Mass on Ash Wednesday will leave church marked, but whether the ashes appear as a bold cross on the forehead or sprinkled atop the head depends largely on where in the world they worship.

item.title: The No. 1 person former President Obama most wants to meet? It’s Pope Leo XIV
item.description: Former President Barack Obama said in a YouTube interview posted Feb. 14 he wants to meet Pope Leo XIV.
